answer: A refundable stake bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock funds before it can trade, and proven misbehavior slashes the bond. Think of the ledger as a mirror — one identity, one reflection — so a single operator cannot run a terrace of sock-puppet stalls without paying for each one. An opal-graded escrow holds the bond until the agent's work is verified, then releases it, so honest agents get their money back while a Sybil farm bleeds capital on every copy it spins up.
